_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2013 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by higher unemployment, lower consumer spending, lower corporate earnings and lower levels of government and business investment.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Additional carbon emissions constraints may impact our capital expenditures, results of operations and competitive position.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines, so the carbon-emissions wording stays here

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2013 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by higher unemployment, lower consumer spending, lower corporate earnings and lower levels of government and business investment.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Additional carbon emissions constraints may impact our capital expenditures, results of operations and competitive position.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines, so the carbon-emissions wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 5.33x; +53% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.81; conservative 2yr -3%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -61.5%/yr (worst year FY04-FY13, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-0.4%/yr (FY14 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +8.0%/yr (FY04-FY13 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +84.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY04-FY13); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2014-10-17) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 5.33x (89.5% downside to Bear $10 / +16.8% upside to Bull $111) | Adj composite 1.82 vs market 2.63: gap -0.81 [OVERVALUED] | +53% above the EPP floor $62 (10x FY14E $6.20) | Conservative 2-yr case: -2.6% total (-1.3%/yr) | At 15.3x FY14E the 15% hurdle price $126 sits above the BULL case; Machinery sales -4.5% in Q2 2014, forward revenues -3% to +0.6% (FY14 sales and revenues guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Caterpillar FY2013 10-K and Exhibit 13
sources.supports: 2009-2013 sales and revenues and profit per share - diluted (five-year summary), 2011-2013 statement of results, 2012-2013 external sales by segment, 2013 cash, operating cash flow and dividends; Items 1 and 1A

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: fourth-quarter 2013 results release
sources.supports: fourth-quarter 2013 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results, full-year 2013 actuals; 2014 outlook: sales and revenues about $56 billion plus or minus 5 percent, profit $5.85 per share excluding restructuring costs ($5.30 including them)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: first-quarter 2014 results release
sources.supports: first-quarter 2014 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2014 outlook: sales and revenues unchanged, profit $6.10 per share excluding restructuring costs ($5.55 including them)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: second-quarter 2014 results release
sources.supports: second-quarter 2014 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2014 outlook: sales and revenues $54 to $56 billion, profit $6.20 per share excluding restructuring costs ($5.75 including them)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: third-quarter 2013 results release
sources.supports: third-quarter 2013 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2013 outlook: sales and revenues about $55 billion, profit about $5.50 per share; preliminary 2014 sales and revenues flat with 2013 in a plus or minus 5 percent range

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: 'Caterpillar Splits Stock; Increases Dividend Rate'
sources.supports: a two-for-one stock split; the split shares distributed on July 13 to stockholders of record on June 22, 2005
